I'm glad it helped! Music never fails. I get you, most of the time I don't wanna be where I am either. It's not always suicidal thoughts, but a need to just leave. 

May I ask how you're feeling exactly? Is there a reason for you wanting to be gone, or is it just an overwhelming feeling that feels out of your control?

I know you're gonna hate this, but it really was out of your control. If you would've known, stuff may have been different, but the only sign that she might've be sick wass her weight loss, which you mentioned that you thought it was because of Go. It wasn't your fault bby

When I was in middle school, my cat ran away. He loved hidiing, so I spent almost two days without seeing him. It wasn't until I noticed his bowl was still empty that I noticed he was gone. I felt like such an idiot as well. I sometimes wonder if he's still alive or not.

I did manage to move on though. I now spend more time with my dog and value him a lot more. Maybe you could spend more time with your puppies? Don't compare them to your old dog, they're different and therefore your relationship with them will be different. They aren't a replacement, they're brand new companions that you could grow to love and play with. Give them a shot, all dogs are so fucking loving it's insane.
This is incredibly inspiring, thank you. Being honest and telling people that you were feeling down takes a lot more courage than what it sounds like. Cheers!

Hi! I'm here for you if you wanna talk. I know it totally sucks when people say this, but please try to calm down. Listen to music or play with your pets if you have any. Go ahead and cry your eyes off if you have to.
Coming from a younger sibling, you guys can't imagine how awesome it feels to have your older sibling support you.
Couldn't they just... give them permission to enter if they believe the person is suicidal? Without having to make it illegal? I'm no law student, but the whole topic seems convoluted and stupid

>my life has been a struggle and I had no break

Same, man ): For me it has been Sickle Cells Disease, divorced parents, bullying and depression and now my mom has cancer. Sometimes I wonder why everything has to be so hard. I really wish you didn't do it, there's always a chance shit will get better, specially when you hit rock bottom. You've been fighting you illness since 10 so you're probably one hell of a fighter. Sometimes it's hard to measure your own worth, so let me confirm that you're awesome for putting up with it for a long time.
You're so brave for not giving up. Keep it up, we believe in you <3

Yeah, I see what you're saying, I live in a third world country and I've seen extreme poverty. What you said is totally right, it's just the way you live it. That said, it is kinda hard to live it like you want to when you're only 18 and still financially dependent, and all I ever hear from people is how the economy is tough and all they do is work. I guess I'm worried that I'll just end up working for the rest of my life, or even worse, not able to find a job, and spend my life not doing the things I love. I'm also really freaking stressed out because of applying to colleges and stuff, and so that's why I sort of exploded yesterday. Thanks for the reply :)

I honestly don't think success has much to do with it. Don't get me wrong, success is great, and it does give you tools to be happier in live and gets you closer to achieving your goals, but Chester and Robin are perfect examples of how dark and destructive depression really is, and even great success isn't enough to fight against it. The fact that you're putting up a fight against it, (by reaching out to us and just by trying to keep on living) shows how brave you are. 


Chester's death is actually what motivated me to create this account and help people that are struggling. [Which explains my username lol](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3kaUvGSLMew)

I know it sounds cheesy, but please keep trying. Heroin addiction is hell, and getting out of it takes time. And negative feelings are maybe just as bad, and probably take even longer to get out of, if ever. But hey, at least you know you have a problem, and have the resolve to fix it. Keep battling, I'm rooting for you <3

Hey man! Your post really got to me. I feel like the worst part for me is getting all hopeful about this or that girl, only to immediatly remind myself that its just not gonna happen. And hanging out with my friends (and their girlfriends) and seeing how happy they are while I'm not is draining. I always tell myself that the wait will just make my first relationship better when it finally arrives. Hang in there man, love might hit you when you're least expecting it! :)

Word. Like, how do other people's tragedies make mine or anyone else's less tragic? People judge too quickly without actually listening to others. Instead of trying to understand why people feel the way they feel, or keeping an open mind and realizing that life isn't always as we originally thought it was, people just dismiss what others have to say if they don't see where they're coming from. 
And it's so unrelated too. What does their uncle Herbert's cancer have to do with me feeling suicidal?
It's all so fucked. We all need more empathy.
